hints: Focus on whether each oxide actually reacts with or dissolves in water, because no reaction means no new H+ or OH- ions.
Recall that CaO is a basic metal oxide that forms Ca(OH)2 in water, while Al2O3 is amphoteric but insoluble.
Check SiO2 next, it is acidic in character but is a giant covalent solid that does not react with water, so only one of the three changes the pH.
walkthrough:
**Ask what changes pH**

Pure water is pH 7. To change it, the oxide must produce $H^+$ ions (acidic, pH < 7) or $OH^-$ ions (basic, pH > 7) in solution.

Rule to use:
$$\text{oxide + water} \rightarrow \text{acid or alkali (if soluble/reactive)}$$

**Test 1: CaO**

CaO is a basic ionic oxide from Group 2. It reacts readily with water to make a sparingly soluble alkali.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CaO(s) + H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$$

**Test 2: Al2O3**

$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric, so it can react with strong acids and strong alkalis, but it is insoluble in water and does not react with water itself.

Result:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\text{ + water } \rightarrow \text{ no reaction, pH stays at 7}$$

**Test 3: SiO2**

$\text{SiO}_2$ is weakly acidic, but it has a giant covalent lattice with very strong Si-O bonds. It does not react with water, only with hot concentrated alkali.

Result:
$$\text{SiO}_2\text{ + water } \rightarrow \text{ no reaction, pH stays at 7}$$

**Conclude the combination**

Only 1 produces $OH^-$ ions and raises the pH above 7. Both 2 and 3 sit unchanged in water.

Deduction: 1 only is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 all change pH. Only CaO does. Al2O3 and SiO2 are insoluble and do not react with water, so they cannot release ions to change pH.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 change pH. While 1 is correct, 2 is not. Students often remember Al2O3 is amphoteric and assume it reacts with water, but amphoteric means reaction with acids and alkalis, not with neutral water.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 change pH. Both are wrong. SiO2 is classed as an acidic oxide, but that acidity only shows with a strong base like NaOH, not with water because its giant covalent structure is unreactive to water.
options.D: Correct. Only 1 is included. CaO reacts to form Ca(OH)2, releasing OH- ions and making the solution alkaline with pH well above 7, while Al2O3 and SiO2 show no reaction with water.
